correctness.rationale: For a right eigenvector the imaginary part of its Rayleigh quotient is minus Gamma times the normalized loss-site weight. A real eigenvector therefore belongs to the clean chain and has a node at the loss; the two cut Jacobi eigenvectors can be joined uniquely at any shared eigenvalue because their endpoint amplitudes cannot vanish. The odd right segment's nonzero squared energies come from its L−1 dimensional Toeplitz block with diagonal a²+b² and off-diagonal ab, and the even left segment's normalized squared-energy determinant is U_u(t)+r U_{u−1}(t), with an endpoint diagonal shift −b². The consecutive U polynomials cannot both vanish, and the left coupling block is invertible, giving the stated positive-ratio test with no zero-mode or endpoint exceptions. Independently of the frozen angle-pair checker, I enumerated all 78 interior (N,s) pairs for N≤14 with a resultant in t against U_{L−1}(t). Its linear factors over the right-hand roots each encode one possible r, or are nonzero constants for vanishing denominators. Exact gcd with its derivative, rational factorization and real-root counts gave repeated positive ratios only at r=1 for N≤13 (at N=7,10,12,13), and r=√2 at N=14,s=3, with multiplicity two. For the infinite family the two right angles are 5π/12 and 11π/12 at every length, and the left block has only four eigenvalues, with squared energies z=a⁻²E²=2±√3. At a=1 and A_1=1 the left norm is 2+2z; each run of 12 right cells contributes 48 since exp(2iθ) has order 12 and the squared sinusoidal amplitude is 4 on each sublattice before averaging. The real modes reduce the lossy operator and the complement decays even with Jordan blocks. Summing the four inverse squared norms gives Eq. (2), including 9/121 at m=1.
